parts: Look at the little square stuck to your monitor. It barely holds on, and that is the whole point.
Peel it off, and it comes away clean. Stick it somewhere else, and it works again.
And, as the usual story goes, it exists because of a glue that was supposed to be strong.
For years, almost nobody knew what to do with it.
So why do sticky notes exist?
In nineteen sixty-eight, a scientist at the company 3M, Spencer Silver, was trying to make a very strong adhesive.
Instead, by accident, he made a weak one. It was low-tack and reusable, and it peeled off without tearing.
A program at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology says it was made of tiny acrylic spheres. Silver hoped it could be a spray, or a surface for bulletin boards.
It was, in Wikipedia's words, a solution without a problem. For about five years, Silver tried to sell the idea inside the company, and few people were interested.
Then came Arthur Fry, a colleague who sang in a church choir. His paper bookmarks kept slipping out of his hymn book.
He thought of Silver's adhesive. A bookmark with that gentle grip could stay in place without tearing the page.
Sources differ on the year of that idea: some say nineteen seventy-three, others nineteen seventy-four.
According to Wikipedia, Fry used a company policy that let employees work on their own projects, and gave samples to his colleagues.
Colleagues began using them to exchange messages. The bookmark had found a second life.
In nineteen seventy-seven, the company test-marketed the product in several cities, under the name Press and Peel.
The results were mixed. Wikipedia calls them disappointing.
A year later, it tried something different: free samples in offices in Boise, Idaho.
According to Wikipedia, about nine in ten people who tried them said they would buy them.
The product was renamed Post-it Note, and in nineteen eighty it went on sale across the United States.
This is the company's story. Not everyone agrees on the credit.
Wikipedia notes that another man, Alan Amron, said he came up with the idea in nineteen seventy-three.
It says his first lawsuit ended in a confidential settlement, and a second one, in twenty sixteen, was dismissed.
We cannot settle that dispute here, so we tell the version in the sources we read, and we note the other.
Next time you use a sticky note, peel it off and stick it somewhere else. That is the failed glue, doing its job.
Here is our reading. The weak grip was a flaw in a glue, and became the feature in a note.
So if you have an idea nobody wants yet, remember this glue. Sometimes the answer already exists, and the question has not been found yet.
A glue that was meant to be strong became famous for being weak.
Everyday objects often hide a simple trick in plain sight. Even the light in your building hallway.
Next time you press the light in a building hallway, notice what happens next. Why does it turn itself off?
